[MAY-015] **RBI Discussion Paper on Digital Payment Safety: 1-Hour Lagged Credit, Kill Switch & ₹25 Lakh Annual Cap**

- **Combating Authorized Push Payment (APP) Frauds**: RBI released a comprehensive Discussion Paper outlining high-friction security interventions to protect retail depositors against social engineering, digital arrest, and APP cyber frauds (which inflicted ₹22,930 crore losses in 2025).
- **1-Hour Lagged Credit on High-Value UPI/IMPS**:
  - Proposes a mandatory **1-hour settlement delay** for all online digital transfers (UPI, IMPS, NEFT) **exceeding ₹10,000**.
  - During this 1-hour escrow window, the sender retains the unilateral legal right to **cancel the transaction**.
  - **Whitelisting Exemption**: Instant real-time settlement permitted without delay if the beneficiary has been pre-registered on the customer's **whitelisted trusted beneficiary list**.
  - **Empirical Rationale**: RBI observed that transactions above ₹10,000 account for **98.5% of total digital fraud value** and **45% of reported cyber fraud cases**.
- **Trusted Person Authentication for Vulnerable Citizens**:
  - Introduces dual-authorization safeguards for **senior citizens aged above 70 years** and **persons with disabilities (PwDs)**.
  - Any digital fund transfer **exceeding ₹50,000** will require secondary approval from a pre-nominated trusted family member or guardian.
- **National Digital 'Kill Switch' & Annual Credit Cap**:
  - **Universal Kill Switch**: Mandates a one-tap emergency Kill Switch across all mobile banking apps to immediately freeze all digital outbound payment channels (modeled on Singapore and Australian protocols).
  - **₹25 Lakh Annual Credit Limit**: Proposes capping aggregate annual credits received by individual and small merchant accounts at **₹25 lakh**; excess funds parked in a holding 'shadow balance' pending KYC reverification.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- UPI Lagged Credit Threshold: Transfers **above ₹10,000** held for **1 hour** (cancellable by sender).
- Fraud Value Concentration: Above ₹10,000 transfers account for **98.5% of fraud value**.
- Senior Citizen Rule: Transfers **above ₹50,000** for citizens **>70 years** require trusted person sign-off.
- Annual Credit Cap: **₹25 lakh** annual incoming credit cap (shadow balance mechanism).
- Emergency Mechanism: One-tap **Digital Kill Switch**.

[MAY-016] **RBI Rationalises Disaster Relief Loan Restructuring: Suo Motu Automatic Restructuring & 135-Day Opt-Out**

- **Framework Notification**: Reserve Bank of India issued revised directions empowering commercial banks and non-banking lenders to deliver immediate credit relief to borrowers struck by natural calamities.
- **Automatic Relief & Suo Motu Restructuring**:
  - Lenders permitted to initiate loan restructuring **suo motu** (without waiting for formal distress applications from borrowers) across areas declared as disaster-hit under the **National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)** or **State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)**.
  - Relief measures include lowering loan interest rates, extending repayment tenures, converting short-term crop loans into medium/long-term term loans, and granting moratoriums.
- **135-Day Borrower Opt-Out Window**:
  - Restructuring applies automatically across all eligible standard loan accounts; affected borrowers are granted a **135-day window from the date of calamity declaration** to opt out if they prefer to service existing repayment terms.
- **Eligibility & Asset Classification Safeguards**:
  - **Standard Account Rule**: Account must be classified as 'Standard' on the date of calamity declaration and not in default for more than **30 days**.
  - **Slippage Upgrade**: Any account that slips into NPA between the calamity declaration date and restructuring implementation will be **upgraded back to 'Standard'** upon execution of the relief plan.
  - **Provisioning**: Banks must maintain an additional specific provision of **5%** on the outstanding debt of restructured borrowers.
  - **Timelines**: Plan invocation within **45 days** of calamity declaration; full implementation within **90 days thereafter**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Suo Motu Authority: Banks and NBFCs can restructure calamity loans **without borrower application**.
- Opt-Out Horizon: Borrowers have **135 days** from calamity declaration to opt out.
- Pre-Condition Default Cap: Not in default for more than **30 days** on calamity date.
- Provisioning Requirement: Additional **5% specific provision** on restructured debt.
- Implementation Window: Invocation within **45 days**; implementation within **90 days**.

[MAY-017] **RBI Mandates Master Direction on Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Framework Effective April 1, 2027**

- **Historic Shift in Credit Provisioning**: RBI formally issued the comprehensive **Master Direction on Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Approach for Bank Loans**, superseding the legacy 40-year-old 'Incurred Loss' provisioning model, effective **April 1, 2027**.
- **Three-Stage Asset Classification & Provisioning Model**:
  - **Stage 1 (Low Credit Risk / Normal)**:
    - Exposures with low or no significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition.
    - Provisioning: **12-month Expected Credit Losses (ECL)**.
    - Minimum statutory floor: At least **0.40%** on secured retail, corporate, and medium enterprise loans; **0.25%** on small/micro enterprises and farm credit; **1.00%** on unsecured retail loans.
  - **Stage 2 (Significant Increase in Credit Risk - SICR)**:
    - Exposures where credit risk has increased significantly since origination, but which are not yet credit-impaired (automatically triggered if payments are **overdue by >30 days**).
    - Provisioning: **Lifetime Expected Credit Losses (Lifetime ECL)**.
    - Minimum statutory floor: **5.00%** provisioning across corporate, retail, and unsecured credit.
  - **Stage 3 (Credit-Impaired / NPAs)**:
    - Defaulted exposures meeting the statutory 90-day delinquency threshold.
    - Provisioning: **Lifetime ECL** (progressively scaling up to **100%** for unsecured exposures depending on age of default).
- **Core Statistical Mechanics & Income Recognition**:
  - ECL computed using econometric formula: $\text{ECL} = \text{Probability of Default (PD)} \times \text{Loss Given Default (LGD)} \times \text{Exposure at Default (EAD)}$.
  - **Borrower-Level Cross-Contamination**: If any single loan facility of a borrower turns NPA, all other credit exposures of that borrower across the bank must be classified as NPA.
  - **Effective Interest Rate (EIR) Transition**: Banks mandated to transition their entire loan books to **Effective Interest Rate (EIR)** accounting by **March 31, 2030**.
  - **Governance**: Supervised by a Board-approved Committee comprising the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Chief Risk Officer (CRO).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Effective Enforcement Date: **April 1, 2027**.
- Transition Milestone: Full transition to Effective Interest Rate (EIR) by **March 31, 2030**.
- Stage 1 Provisioning: **12-Month ECL** (0.40% secured, 0.25% MSME/agri, 1.00% unsecured retail).
- Stage 2 Trigger: Overdue by **>30 days**; requires **Lifetime ECL** (minimum **5.00%**).
- Stage 3 Trigger: Overdue by **>90 days**; requires **Lifetime ECL** (up to **100%**).
- Quantitative Formula: $\text{PD} \times \text{LGD} \times \text{EAD}$.

[MAY-018] **RBI Mandates Global Reporting of All Rupee OTC Foreign Exchange Derivatives to CCIL**

- **FX Derivatives Transparency Overhaul**: Reserve Bank of India instituted a sweeping reporting reform mandating Authorised Dealer Category-I (**AD Cat-I**) banks to report all **Over-the-Counter (OTC) Foreign Exchange (FX) Derivative Contracts involving the Indian Rupee (INR)**.
- **Reporting Repository & Global Extraterritoriality**:
  - All transactions must be reported to the trade repository of the **Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL)**.
  - Extends extraterritorially: Covers OTC Rupee derivative contracts executed anywhere in the world by the bank's **parent company, overseas branches, and foreign subsidiaries/related entities**.
  - Captures both **Deliverable** and **Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF)** contracts.
- **Three-Phase Progressive Implementation Timetable**:
  - **Phase 1 (Effective July 1, 2027)**: Mandatory reporting of **100% of contracts** entered into by the **parent bank entities**.
  - **Phase 2 (Effective January 1, 2028)**: Reporting of at least **70% of total notional trade value** executed by other related entities / overseas arms (progressively stepping up to **80%**).
  - **Phase 3 (Effective July 1, 2028)**: Full compliance mandated — **100% of notional trade value** across all global related entities must be reported.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Mandatory Trade Repository: **Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL)**.
- Phase 1 Deadline: **July 1, 2027** (100% of parent entity contracts).
- Phase 2 Deadline: **January 1, 2028** (70%–80% notional value of related entities).
- Phase 3 Full Enforcement: **July 1, 2028** (100% notional value worldwide).
- Instruments Covered: Both **Deliverable and Non-Deliverable OTC Rupee FX Derivatives**.

[MAY-021] **PFRDA Rolls Out Retirement Income Schemes (RIS) with Systematic Payout (SPR) and Unit Redemption (SUR)**

- **Post-Retirement Pension Innovation**: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (**PFRDA**, established under PFRDA Act, 2013; Chairman: **Sivasubramanian Ramann**) launched **Retirement Income Schemes (RIS)** under the National Pension System (**NPS**).
- **Addressing Superannuation Inflexibility**:
  - Subscribers reaching 60 years previously had to mandatorily annuitize at least 40% of their accumulated corpus and withdraw the remaining 60% as a lump sum.
  - RIS permits retirees who do not require an immediate lump sum to remain invested in NPS up to the **age of 75 or 85 years**, drawing structured, tax-efficient regular income.
- **Two Flexible Post-Retirement Withdrawal Pathways**:
  1. **Systematic Payout Rate (SPR)**:
     - The payout rate is calibrated dynamically based on the subscriber's current age and chosen drawdown end-age.
     - For a subscriber exiting at age 60 and selecting an 85-year drawdown horizon, the initial annual payout begins at **4.00%**, resetting annually on the subscriber's date of birth based on the prevailing net market value of the fund corpus.
     - Any residual corpus at the end of the drawdown horizon can be withdrawn as a lump sum or merged into an annuity.
  2. **Systematic Unit Redemption (SUR)**:
     - The subscriber's total accumulated units are divided evenly across the chosen drawdown tenure.
     - A **fixed number of mutual units are redeemed every month**, providing an automated monthly cashflow irrespective of fluctuations in daily Net Asset Value (NAV).
- **NPS Regulatory Landmarks**:
  - Open to all Indian citizens (residents, NRIs, and OCIs) aged **18 to 85 years** on a voluntary basis.
  - Asset allocation spans 4 standardized classes: **Equity (Class E), Corporate Bonds (Class C), Government Securities (Class G), and Alternative Investment Funds (Class A)**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Regulating Body: **PFRDA** (Chairman: **Sivasubramanian Ramann**; HQ: New Delhi).
- Scheme Name: **Retirement Income Schemes (RIS)** under NPS.
- Maximum Drawdown Age: Permitted up to **85 years** (extended from age 75).
- Two Withdrawal Mechanics: **Systematic Payout Rate (SPR)** and **Systematic Unit Redemption (SUR)**.
- SPR Benchmark Payout: Starts at **4% p.a.** for age 60-to-85 drawdown (resets annually on birth date).
- NPS Voluntary Entry Age: **18 to 85 years**.

- **Regulatory Framework & Mandate**: Reserve Bank of India issued an amendment to the *Master Direction – RBI (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025*, significantly easing capital requirements for bank loans backed by the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (**ECLGS 5.0**).
- **Split Risk-Weight Mechanism**:
  - **75% of the Guaranteed Portion**: Attracts a **0% risk weight**, meaning banks are completely exempt from setting aside regulatory capital against this portion of the exposure.
  - **Remaining 25% Exposure**: Attracts a concessional **20% risk weight** (drastically reduced from standard unrated exposure weights).
- **Settlement Condition for 0% Weight**:
  - Banks can avail of the 0% risk weight benefit **only if** the guarantee claim is settled within **30 days** from the date of invocation.
  - If the 30-day settlement requirement is breached, the benefit of the 0% risk weight is revoked, and standard capital charges apply.
- **Strategic Intent**: Designed to release trapped bank capital, incentivize fresh liquidity flow to distressed and contact-intensive businesses, and align sovereign-backed portfolio risk with Basel III Pillar 1 norms.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Risk-Weight Split: **0% on 75%** of guaranteed portion vs **20% on remaining 25%** (a classic matching/statement MCQ).
- Time Boundary for Settlement: Must be settled within **30 days** of claim invocation to retain 0% risk weight.
- Policy Anchor: Governed under the *RBI (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions*.

[JUN-003] **Credit Guarantee Scheme for Microfinance Institutions 2.0 (CGSMFI-2.0): Expansion to ₹20,000 Crore Pool**

- **Framework Evolution**: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services – DFS) and NCGTC operationalized **CGSMFI-2.0**, transitioning from emergency COVID-era relief (launched 28 June 2021) into a permanent, risk-based, tier-structured credit enhancement framework.
- **Pool Size & Validity**:
  - Total guarantee pool expanded to **₹20,000 crore**.
  - Extended validity up to **31 August 2026** (or until the ₹20,000 Cr guarantees are fully exhausted).
- **NCGTC Institutional Profile**:
  - Implemented by **National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC)**, set up under DFS, Ministry of Finance (established in Union Budget 2013-14; incorporated 28 March 2014 under Companies Act 1956; paid-up capital **₹10 crore**; Headquartered in Mumbai).
- **Three-Tier MFI Classification & Loan Limits**:
  - **Small-size MFIs (AUM < ₹500 crore)**: Max loan capacity capped at **20% of AUM, subject to a maximum of ₹100 crore**; NCGTC guarantee cover of **80%**; mandatory bank allocation of minimum 5% of bank's scheme pool.
  - **Medium-size MFIs (AUM ₹500 crore to < ₹2,000 crore)**: Max loan capacity capped at **20% of AUM, subject to a maximum of ₹200 crore**; NCGTC guarantee cover of **75%**; mandatory bank allocation of minimum 10% of bank's scheme pool.
  - **Large-size MFIs (AUM ≥ ₹2,000 crore)**: Max loan capacity enhanced upward from ₹300 crore to **₹1,000 crore** (subject to 20% of AUM); NCGTC guarantee cover of **70%**; eligible for remaining available pool.

  - **On-Lending Rate to Borrowers**: Capped at **1.0% below** the MFI's average lending rate of the preceding six months.
- **Guarantee Fee & Utilization**:
  - Guarantee fee fixed at **0.50% per annum** on the sanctioned amount in the 1st year, and on outstanding balance from Year 2 onwards.
  - Minimum **80% of funds** must be deployed for fresh microfinance loan assets within **4 months**.

- Large MFI Max Loan Ceiling: Enhanced from ₹300 Cr to **₹1,000 crore** (capped at 20% of AUM).
- Tier-wise Guarantee Cover: Small = **80%**, Medium = **75%**, Large = **70%**.
- Interest Spread Cap: Lending to MFIs capped at **EBLR/MCLR + 2%**; on-lending capped at **1% below** average rate.

[JUN-004] **RBI Master Directions on Bank Lending to REITs & InvITs (49% Aggregate Exposure Cap)**

- **Policy Harmonization**: RBI released the *Master Directions on Bank Lending to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)*, permitting scheduled commercial banks to lend directly to business trusts under strict prudential boundaries.
- **Eligibility & Asset Composition Norms**:
  - Banks can lend **only to SEBI-registered and publicly listed** REITs and InvITs.
  - **Operational Asset Threshold**: At least **80% of the underlying assets** of the borrowing REIT/InvIT must comprise completed, revenue-generating properties/infrastructure projects that have yielded positive cash flows for **more than one year**.
- **Aggregate Lending & Exposure Limits**:
  - **Aggregate Bank Exposure Cap**: Total lending across all commercial banks to any single borrowing REIT or InvIT (including its SPVs and holding companies) must not exceed **49% of the value of the trust's total assets**.
  - **Funding Restriction**: Bank loans to REITs/InvITs **cannot** be utilized to fund underlying Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) that are already facing financial distress or have existing non-performing loans with regulated entities.
- **Risk Weights & Governance**:
  - Exposure to REITs attracts a **100% risk weight** (**125%** if categorized as capital market exposure).
  - Exposure to InvITs attracts corporate lending risk weights based on external credit ratings.
  - Board-approved policies mandatory; statutory migration to a comprehensive capital charge framework effective **1 April 2027**.
- **Statutory Effective Date**: Directions take effect from **1 October 2026** (banks permitted voluntary early adoption).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Aggregate Exposure Cap: **≤49%** of the value of the trust's total assets (NOT 50% or 75%).
- Completed Asset Requirement: Minimum **80%** completed and revenue-generating with >1 year positive cash flow.
- Capital Charge Migration Date: **1 April 2027**; General compliance effective **1 October 2026**.

[JUN-005] **RBI Master Directions on Authorisation of Payment System Operators (PSOs) — Perpetual Licences & Governance**

- **Statutory Authority**: Issued under **Section 4 of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007**, governing entities seeking to operate payment systems in India.
- **Perpetual Validity Regime**:
  - All fresh Certificates of Authorisation (CoA) granted to PSOs will carry **perpetual validity** (eliminating the earlier 5-year periodic renewal requirement).
  - Existing authorized PSOs will be transitioned to perpetual validity at the time of their next renewal, subject to complete regulatory compliance.
  - **Non-Compliant Entities**: PSOs exhibiting governance or operational deficiencies will receive conditional renewals for a **limited period of 1 year only**, until deficiencies are fully rectified.
- **FDI & Foreign Investment from FATF Non-Compliant Jurisdictions**:
  - Investments from jurisdictions non-compliant with Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards will not be treated at par with compliant countries.
  - Fresh investments from FATF non-compliant jurisdictions must account for **less than 20% of the voting power** of the PSO in aggregate.
- **Surrender of Certificate & Cooling-Off Period**:
  - Surrendering a CoA requires a written application to DPSS Central Office, accompanied by a **Statutory Auditor's certificate** confirming all customer, merchant, and bank liabilities are fully settled.
  - A mandatory **one-year cooling-off period** is imposed before an entity can re-apply if its CoA was revoked, renewal was rejected, or licence was surrendered.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Licence Validity: **Perpetual validity** for compliant PSOs; **1 year only** for non-compliant entities.
- FATF Non-Compliant Voting Cap: Must remain strictly **below 20%** of aggregate voting power.
- Cooling-Off Duration: **1 year** from revocation, surrender, or application rejection.

[JUN-007] **RBI Revamped Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme Directions 2026: Collateral-Free Limit Raised to ₹2 Lakh**

- **Comprehensive Overhaul**: RBI issued the *Reserve Bank of India (Kisan Credit Card – KCC) Directions, 2026*, applying to all Scheduled Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, RRBs, and Rural Co-operative Banks, taking effect from **1 January 2027** (existing loans continue till maturity/renewal).
- **Enhanced Collateral-Free Exemption Limit**:
  - Banks mandated to waive collateral security and margin requirements for agricultural loans up to **₹2 lakh per borrower** (raised from the earlier ₹1.60 lakh threshold).
  - Exemption equally covers allied agricultural activities (dairy, poultry, fisheries, animal husbandry).
  - Voluntary pledge of gold/silver ornaments for loans up to ₹2 lakh is permitted and will **not** be treated as a violation of collateral-free guidelines.
  - KCC loans up to **₹3 lakh** secured via hypothecation of crops or assets under formal tie-up recovery arrangements may also be exempted from collateral.
- **Standardized Crop Seasons**:
  - **Short-duration crops**: Standardized strictly to **12 months** (period from raising crop to harvesting and marketing).
  - **Long-duration crops**: Standardized strictly to **18 months**.
- **Flexi KCC for Marginal Farmers**:
  - Revolving credit facility between **₹10,000 to ₹50,000** designed for marginal farmers (landholding up to 1 hectare) based on land and cropping pattern, without requiring complex cost-of-cultivation documentation.
- **Term Loan Component Repayment Horizon**:
  - Investment credit/term loan portion under KCC is repayable within a maximum of **6 years** (if asset life/repayment requires >6 years, it must be treated as a separate loan facility outside KCC).
- **Maximum Permissible Limit (MPL)**:
  - Sanctioned limit based on scale of finance + 10% for post-harvest/household + 20% for maintenance/repairs.
  - For 2nd crop season onwards, MPL is notionally increased by **10% per annum** over the previous crop season's limit.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Collateral-Free Limit: **₹2 lakh per borrower** (enhanced from ₹1.60 lakh).
- Standardized Crop Seasons: Short-duration = **12 months**; Long-duration = **18 months**.
- Term Loan Under KCC: Maximum repayment tenor **6 years** (longer loans must sit outside KCC).
- Flexi KCC Limits: **₹10,000 to ₹50,000** for marginal farmers (holding ≤1 hectare).
- Effective Date: **1 January 2027**.

[JUN-008] **RBI Revamps Lead Bank Scheme (LBS): 60% CD Ratio Benchmark & 3-Tier Governance**

- **Framework Background**: RBI issued revised comprehensive guidelines for the **Lead Bank Scheme (LBS)** (first introduced in 1969 following the Gadgil Study Group and Nariman Committee recommendations).
- **Key Administrative Designations**:
  - **Lead District Manager (LDM)**: Lead Bank must appoint an exclusive officer as LDM for each designated district (assignment of multiple districts to one LDM barred except in exceptional circumstances).
  - **District Development Manager (DDM)**: Appointed by **NABARD** in every district to liaise between district administration and financial institutions.
  - **Lead District Officer (LDO)**: Appointed by the **Reserve Bank of India** for each district to supervise credit flow.
  - **SLBC Convenor**: Convenor bank in every State/UT must designate an officer not below the rank of **General Manager (GM)** as SLBC Convenor.
- **Three-Tier Governance Structure**:
  1. *Tier 1 (Block Level)*: Block Level Bankers' Committees (**BLBCs**).
  2. *Tier 2 (District Level)*: District Consultative Committees (**DCCs**) and District Level Review Committees (DLRCs).
  3. *Tier 3 (State Level)*: State Level Bankers' Committees (**SLBCs** / UTLBCs).
- **Credit-Deposit (CD) Ratio Benchmarks & Corrective Action**:
  - Baseline Target: Minimum **60% CD Ratio** for rural and semi-urban branches on an all-India basis.
  - **CD Ratio between 40% and 60%**: Monitored by the District Consultative Committee (DCC) for step-up improvement.
  - **CD Ratio below 40%**: Mandatorily reviewed by a **Special Sub-Committee (SSC)** under DCC, chaired by the District Collector with LDM as Convenor.
  - **CD Ratio below 20%**: District placed under the **Special Category Districts** for rigorous monthly monitoring and structural intervention.
  - Similar Special Sub-Committees constituted if Annual Credit Plan (ACP) achievement falls **below 100%**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- CD Ratio Thresholds: Ideal target = **60%**; Special Sub-Committee review triggered at **<40%**; Special Category status triggered at **<20%**.
- Rank of SLBC Convenor: Not below **General Manager (GM)**.
- Lead Bank Inception: Introduced in **1969** based on Nariman Committee / F.K.F. Nariman recommendations.

[JUN-010] **RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Balance Sheet Surges 20.6% to ₹91.97 Lakh Crore & ₹2.89 Lakh Crore Surplus Transfer**

- **Statutory Submission**: Submitted by the Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India to the Central Government under **Section 53(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** (reporting period: **April 2025 – March 2026**).
- **Balance Sheet Expansion**:
  - Total balance sheet size expanded by **20.6%** (an absolute increase of **₹15,71,699.15 crore**), rising from ₹76,25,421.93 crore as on March 31, 2025 to **₹91,97,121.08 crore** as on March 31, 2026.
  - **Balance Sheet-to-GDP Ratio**: Stood at **26.4%** of India's GDP as of end-March 2026 (up from 23.7% a year ago).
  - Initial paid-up capital of the Reserve Bank remains at **₹5 crore** (constituted as a private shareholders bank in 1935, fully nationalised on January 1, 1949).
- **Surplus Transfer & Contingent Risk Buffer (CRB)**:
  - **Surplus Transfer to Central Government**: RBI approved a total surplus transfer of **₹2,88,588.45 crore** (₹2.89 lakh crore) for FY26 (up 7.3% from ₹2,68,588.07 crore in FY25). Total available balance was ₹2,88,592.45 crore (with ₹4 crore statutory contributions: ₹1 crore each to National Industrial Credit Long Term Operations Fund, National Housing Credit LTO Fund, and ₹1 crore each transferable to NABARD for National Rural Credit LTO Fund and National Rural Credit Stabilisation Fund).
  - **Economic Capital Framework (ECF / Bimal Jalan Committee)**: Mandates CRB within **4.5% to 7.5%** of balance sheet. The Central Board approved maintaining the CRB at the upper cap of **6.5%**.
  - **Contingency Fund (CF) Allocation**: RBI made a provision of **₹1,09,379.64 crore** (~₹1.09 lakh crore) transferred to CF during the year. No provision was made towards Asset Development Fund (ADF).
- **Asset Composition & Financial Performance**:
  - **Total Income**: Increased by **26.4%**, while total expenditure rose by **102.4%**.
  - **Foreign Assets (70.9%)**: Foreign investments rose 7.9% to ₹52.68 lakh crore; sovereign gold holdings jumped **63.8%** to ₹10.94 lakh crore. Net sale of foreign exchange stood at **USD 53.13 billion**, yielding net exchange gains of **₹1.69 lakh crore**.
  - **Domestic Assets (29.1%)**: Rose 44.9% to ₹22.59 lakh crore. Rupee securities interest income grew 37.7% to ₹1.18 lakh crore.
  - **Liabilities Breakdown**: Revaluation accounts (+63.4%), Notes issued (+11.8%), Deposits (+11.6%), Other liabilities (+21.1%).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Total Balance Sheet Size: **₹91,97,121.08 crore** (+20.6% YoY growth; **26.4% of GDP**).
- Surplus Transferred to GoI: **₹2,88,588.45 crore** (FY25: ₹2,68,588.07 crore).
- Provision to Contingency Fund (CF): **₹1,09,379.64 crore** (CRB pegged at **6.5%**; ECF band: 4.5%–7.5%).
- Section Applied: Section 53(2) for Annual Report submission; initial capital remains ₹5 crore (nationalised Jan 1, 1949).

[JUN-011] **RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Currency Management, Counterfeits (FICNs) & Digital Rupee (e₹)**

- **Banknotes & Coins in Circulation**:
  - **Banknotes in Circulation (BiC)**: Increased by **11.9% in value** and **10.5% in volume** during 2025–26.
  - **Highest Denomination Share**: In volume terms, the **₹500 denomination** constituted the highest share of total banknotes in circulation, followed by the **₹10 denomination**.
  - **Coins in Circulation**: Total value increased by **11.4%**, while volume expanded by **4.5%**. Coins of ₹1, ₹2, and ₹5 together constituted **80.7% of total volume** and **60.2% of total value**.
  - **₹2000 Note Withdrawal Status**: As of March 31, 2026, **98.45%** of the ₹3.56 lakh crore worth of ₹2000 banknotes in circulation at the time of the withdrawal announcement (May 19, 2023) had returned to the banking system. Facility remains active across 19 RBI Issue Offices.
- **Central Bank Digital Currency (e₹)**:
  - Total e₹ (CBDC) in circulation stood at **₹771.7 crore** as on March 31, 2026.
  - Retail programmable CBDC pilots successfully credited food subsidies to Public Distribution System (PDS) beneficiaries across **Gujarat, Puducherry, and Chandigarh**.
  - RBI launched the **Unified Markets Interface (UMI)** to facilitate tokenisation of financial assets using wholesale CBDC (first pilot launched on **Certificates of Deposit - CDs**).
  - Bilateral cross-border CBDC discussions/MoUs held with **Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)** and **Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE)**; joined BIS Innovation Hub's **Project Rialto** and **Project Mandala (Phase 2)**.
- **Counterfeit Currency (FICNs) Detection**:
  - **Share of Detection**: Only **2.4%** of total Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICNs) detected across the banking sector were detected at the Reserve Bank of India; **97.6%** were detected by commercial banks.
  - **Denomination Trends**: Counterfeit notes detected in ₹10, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, and ₹2000 denominations registered a marked decline; counterfeit ₹500 notes increased by **20.5%** and ₹20 notes increased by **47.4%**.
  - **Currency Infrastructure & Awareness**: **State Bank of India (SBI)** accounted for the highest share of Currency Chests across India. RBI replaced its legacy 'Paisa Bolta Hai' portal with the comprehensive **Indian Currency Microsite** on September 10, 2025. Print trials of varnished banknotes were conducted at **BRBNMPL Mysuru Press**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Total CBDC (e₹) in Circulation: **₹771.7 crore** (as of March 31, 2026).
- ₹2000 Note Return Rate: **98.45%** of ₹3.56 lakh crore total value returned.
- FICN Detection Share: Reserve Bank detected **2.4%**; Commercial Banks detected **97.6%**.
- Banknote Value/Volume Growth: Value grew **11.9%**; Volume grew **10.5%** (₹500 note leads volume share).
- Largest Currency Chest Holder: **State Bank of India (SBI)**.

[JUN-012] **RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Bank Frauds, Supervisory Reforms & Regulatory Modernisation**

- **Systemic Fraud Surge**:
  - Total fraud amount surged **46% to ₹48,021 crore** in 2025–26 (from ₹32,803 crore in FY25), even as total reported fraud incidents fell by more than half to 10,114 cases.
  - **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)**: Accounted for **74.5%** of total fraud value (**₹35,709 crore** across 3,000+ cases; average fraud size ₹6.6 crore).
  - **Private Sector Banks**: Accounted for **23.7%** (₹11,399 crore).
  - **Dominant Segment**: **Loan Advances** accounted for **85%** of total fraud value (**₹40,774 crore** across 8,640 cases).
- **Consolidation of Regulations Exercise**:
  - To streamline compliance, more than **11,000 circulars and instructions** were consolidated into **244 Master Directions (MDs)** covering 30 functional areas across 11 classes of Regulated Entities (REs), repealing **9,445 circulars**.
  - RBI also released **64 draft master directions** across 9 functional supervisory areas.
- **Deposit Insurance & Supervisory Governance**:
  - **DICGC Premium**: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (established under DICGC Act, 1961) maintained a flat-rate premium of **₹0.12 (12 paise) per ₹100 per annum** (0.12% p.a.) on assessable deposits; coverage limit intact at **₹5 lakh** per depositor per bank.
  - **Risk-Based Premium (RBP) Framework**: Introduced effective **April 1, 2026**, establishing a 2-tier risk-based rating methodology (Tier 1: SCBs other than RRBs; Tier 2: RRBs, rural co-op banks, and UCBs).
  - **Registered Insured Banks**: Stood at **1,950** as of March 31, 2026 (124 commercial banks including 11 SFBs, 6 PBs, 28 RRBs, 2 LABs; and 1,826 co-operative banks).
  - **Supervisory Data Quality Index (sDQI)**: Published on a **quarterly** basis under Utkarsh 2.0.
  - **Co-Lending Framework Revision**: Reduced minimum loan share retention by Regulated Entities from 20% to **10%**, and extended First Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) coverage up to **5%**.
- **AI Governance & FinTech Architecture**:
  - **FREE-AI Framework**: RBI formulated the *Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence* anchored on **7 Sutras** and **6 Strategic Pillars** (26 recommendations: 13 on innovation enablement, 13 on risk mitigation).
  - **MuleHunter.ai™**: AI/ML supervised model developed by RBI Innovation Hub (RBIH) to identify mule bank accounts in near-real time.
  - **Digital Payment Intelligence Platform (DPIP)**: Established as a collaborative network-level digital intelligence utility to combat payment fraud.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Consolidation of Regulations: **11,000+ circulars** condensed into **244 Master Directions**; 9,445 repealed.
- DICGC Flat Premium: **0.12% per annum** (12 paise per ₹100); RBP framework effective **April 1, 2026**.
- Co-Lending Retention Minimum: Lowered to **10%** (FLDG cover up to **5%**).
- FREE-AI Architecture: **7 Sutras** + **6 Pillars** + **26 Recommendations**; Mule detector = **MuleHunter.ai™**.
- Total System Frauds: **₹48,021 crore** (PSBs = 74.5%; Advances = ₹40,774 crore / 85%).

- **Monetary Policy Operations & Corridors**:

  - **Training & Infrastructure**: Reserve Bank Staff College (RBSC) located in **Chennai**; College of Agricultural Banking (CAB) in **Pune**; College of Supervisors (CoS) in **Mumbai**; ECCTI in **Bhubaneswar**.

[JUN-015] **RBI Introduces Special USD-Rupee Forex Swap Facilities to Attract Capital Inflows**

- **Twin Forex Swap Windows**: To stabilize the Rupee against crude oil volatility and encourage foreign currency inflows, RBI introduced two concessional USD-INR forex swap facilities:
  1. *FCNR(B) Window*: For fresh **Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank [FCNR(B)]** deposits of 3 to 5 years maturity.
  2. *ECB/OFCB Window*: For fresh External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) and Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) raised by AD Category-I banks (maturity ≥3 years).
- **Concessional Pricing & Tenor**:
  - **Fixed Swap Rate**: Swaps executed at a fixed rate of **1.5% per annum** (compounded semi-annually), significantly below prevailing market hedging rates.
  - **Tenor**: Aligned with borrowing maturity, capped at a maximum of **5 years**.
  - **Operational Windows**: FCNR(B) swap window open till **16 October 2026** (deposits mobilized up to 30 Sept 2026); ECB/OFCB window open till **15 January 2027** (inflows up to 31 Dec 2026).
- **Statutory Reserve Exemptions & NOP-INR Relief**:
  - Eligible FCNR(B) deposits mobilized under this scheme are **exempt from CRR (3.0%) and SLR (18.0%)** requirements.
  - RBI **exempted swap positions from Net Open Position in Rupee (NOP-INR) limits** (which restricts banks' onshore deliverable positions to USD 100 million at end of day), allowing banks to swap up to hundreds of millions without breaching exposure caps.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Fixed Swap Rate: **1.5% per annum** compounded semi-annually.
- Statutory Exemptions: Fresh FCNR(B) deposits under the scheme are **exempt from CRR and SLR**.
- NOP-INR Rule: Banks are normally subject to a **\$100 million Net Open Position** deliverable cap, which is waived for these swaps.

[JUN-016] **Ministry of Finance & RBI Reform FPI Debt Framework: Capital Gains Exemption & PROI Limit Hike**

- **Income-Tax Exemption on Sovereign Debt**:
  - Central Government notified that tax liability for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs/FIIs) on specified Government Securities (G-Secs) investments is **reduced to Nil** effective **1 April 2026**.
  - Both **interest income and capital gains** (earlier Short-Term Capital Gains taxed at 30%, Long-Term at 12.5%) earned from specified G-Secs are completely exempt from tax.
  - Similar comprehensive tax exemption extended to the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)**.
- **Liberalisation for Persons Resident Outside India (PROI)**:
  - Permitted individual **Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs)** (including non-NRIs/OCIs) to invest in listed Indian equity through the Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS).
  - **Individual Limit**: Increased from 5% to **10%** of the paid-up equity capital of an Indian company.
  - **Aggregate Limit**: Increased from 10% to **24%** for all PROIs combined.
- **FPI Limits under General Route Rationalized**:
  - Short-term investment limit (earlier capped at 30% for securities with residual maturity up to 1 year) **completely removed**.
  - Concentration limits (earlier 10% to 15% per corporate debt issuer) **completely removed**.
  - Retained quantitative sovereign caps: **6.0%** of outstanding stock in Central G-Secs and **2.0%** in State Development Loans (SDLs).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- FPI G-Sec Tax Rate: Reduced to **Nil** from 1 April 2026 (both interest and capital gains).
- PROI Equity Investment Caps: Individual limit raised to **10%** (from 5%); Aggregate limit raised to **24%** (from 10%).
- FPI G-Sec Stock Caps: **6%** for Central Government Securities, **2%** for SDLs.

---44:T1c7d,[JUN-023] **SEBI Revises Trading Framework for ETFs: Dynamic Price Bands & Pre-Open Auction**

- **Regulatory Directive**: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) revamped the trading framework for **Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)**, taking effect from **1 September 2026**, replacing the rigid 20% fixed NAV price band.
- **Dynamic Price Band Architecture**:
  - **Equity & Debt ETFs**: Initial dynamic price band set at **10%**. If touched, a cooling-off period is triggered, followed by phased expansions in **increments of 5% up to a maximum of 20%**.
  - **Overnight & Liquid ETFs**: Completely **excluded** from dynamic price bands.
- **Commodity ETFs (Gold & Silver ETFs)**:
  - Initial dynamic price band set at **±6%**.
  - Expandable in stages of **3%** following a cooling-off period, with **no upper or lower limit** on total price expansions during a trading session to mirror global bullion market volatility.
- **Base Price Determination via VWAP**:
  - ETF base price determined using the **Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP)** of trades executed during the **last 30 minutes** of the previous trading day.
- **Pre-Open Call Auction Mechanism**:
  - Introduced a dedicated Pre-Open Call Auction session specifically for **commodity ETFs** to ensure fair price discovery prior to regular market open.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Initial Dynamic Price Bands: **10%** for Equity/Debt ETFs (max 20%); **±6%** for Commodity Gold/Silver ETFs (expandable by 3%, no cap).
- Excluded Categories: **Overnight and Liquid ETFs**.
- Base Price Formula: VWAP of the **last 30 minutes** of trading.
- Effective Date: **1 September 2026**.

[JUN-042] **WPI Base Year Revision to 2022-23: DPIIT Introduces Targeted Mean Imputation for Missing Prices**

- **Statistical Modernization**: Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry) finalized the methodology for transitioning the **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** from the 2011-12 base to the new **2022-23 base year**.
- **Methodological Breakthrough**:
  - Replaces the legacy **"Carry Forward" method** (which duplicated the previous month's price when data was missing) with **"Targeted Mean Imputation"**.
  - Imputes missing commodity quotations using the weighted average price trend of closely related items within the same commodity group, eliminating artificial price stickiness.
- **May 2026 Inflation Readings**:
  - Headline WPI inflation recorded at **9.68%** (all-India Index at 109.9).
  - WPI Food Index inflation stood at **4.49%**.
- **Administrative Anchor**: DPIIT Secretary **Amardeep Singh Bhatia** confirmed the parallel run of the new series before final sunsetting of the 2011-12 index.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- New WPI Target Base Year: **2022-23** (replacing 2011-12).
- New Price Imputation Technique: **Targeted Mean Imputation** (replaces Carry Forward method).
- May 2026 Print: Headline WPI at **9.68%**; Food Index at **4.49%**.
- Issuing Office: **Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT** (Ministry of Commerce and Industry).

- **Historic Precedent**: Department of Commerce (Ministry of Commerce & Industry) granted formal approval for two new Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in the Union Territory of Puducherry, creating an institutional first in urban governance.
- **Two Approved SEZs**:
  - **Thattanchavady IT/ITES SEZ**: Developed directly by the **Oulgaret Municipality** — marking the **first-ever Special Economic Zone in India developed and managed by an Urban Local Body (ULB) / Municipality**.
  - **Karasur Multi-Sector SEZ**: Developed by the Puducherry Industrial Promotion Development and Investment Corporation (**PIPDIC**) across 150 acres to drive advanced manufacturing.
- **National Health Accounts (NHA) FY23 Benchmarks**:
  - Total Health Expenditure (**THE**) reached **₹8.81 Lakh Crore** (**3.37% of GDP**; ₹6,242 per capita).
  - **Government Health Expenditure (GHE)** surged to **1.43% of GDP** (accounting for **48.0% of THE**, up sharply from 28.6% in FY14).
  - **Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE)** plunged to **39.4% of THE** (down from 64.2% in FY14).
  - Private Health Insurance (PHI) increased its share in THE from 3.4% (2013-14) to **9.2% (2022-23)**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- First Urban Local Body/Municipality in India to Develop an SEZ: **Oulgaret Municipality, Puducherry** (at Thattanchavady).
- Multi-Sector SEZ Agency: **PIPDIC** at Karasur.
- NHA FY23 GHE as % of GDP: **1.43%** (GHE share of THE = **48.0%**).
- NHA FY23 OOPE as % of THE: **39.4%** (historic reduction from 64.2%).

- **Aviation Safety Deployment**: Ministry of Earth Sciences (**MoES**) operationalized **'SkyCast'**, an indigenous, high-resolution fog and low-cloud numerical prediction system engineered specifically for airport operations.
- **Technical & Research Heritage**:
  - Built upon extensive observational data from the **Winter Fog Experiment (WiFEX)** conducted by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (**IITM, Pune**) and the India Meteorological Department (**IMD**).

  - Target: Up to **50% improvement in weather forecasting accuracy** across cyclones, heatwaves, monsoon depressions, and aviation visibility.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- SkyCast Research Origin: **WiFEX experiment** conducted by **IITM Pune & IMD**.
- Airports Deployed: **IGI Delhi** and expanding to **Noida International Airport (Jewar)**.
- Mission Mausam Financial Outlay: **₹2,000 crore** (2024–2026) under MoES.
- Forecast Accuracy Improvement Goal: Up to **50% enhancement**.

[JUN-046] **PM SVANidhi Revised Norms: Tranche Caps Raised to ₹15k/₹25k & RuPay Credit Card Rollout**

- **Scheme Enhancements**: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (**MoHUA**) notified revised operational guidelines for the Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (**PM SVANidhi**), enhancing collateral-free working capital thresholds.
- **Upgraded Three-Tranche Credit Architecture**:
  - **1st Tranche**: Working capital loan limit increased from ₹10,000 to **₹15,000** (tenor: 12 months).
  - **2nd Tranche**: Working capital loan limit increased from ₹20,000 to **₹25,000** (tenor: 18 months) upon timely repayment of tranche 1.
  - **3rd Tranche**: Working capital loan capped at **₹50,000** (tenor: 36 months).
- **UPI-Linked RuPay Credit Card**:
  - Street vendors who successfully repay their 2nd tranche loan and become eligible for the 3rd tranche receive an interoperable **UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card**.
  - Credit limit starts at **₹10,000** and can be stepped up to **₹30,000** based on digital transaction history; card validity is **5 years**.
- **'Samadhan Didi' AI Grievance Chatbot**:
  - MoS (IC) Dr. Jitendra Singh launched **'Samadhan Didi'**, an AI-enabled multilingual voice chatbot for the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (**CPGRAMS**) at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- 1st Tranche Loan Limit: Raised to **₹15,000** (repayable in 12 months).
- 2nd Tranche Loan Limit: Raised to **₹25,000** (repayable in 18 months).
- 3rd Tranche Loan Limit: **₹50,000** (repayable in 36 months).
- RuPay Credit Card Limit for Street Vendors: **₹10,000 to ₹30,000** (validity: **5 years**).
- CPGRAMS AI Voice Chatbot: **'Samadhan Didi'** (MoPPG&P).

[JUN-047] **Surha Taal Bird Sanctuary Designated as Ramsar Wetland: India Ranks 1st in Asia & 3rd Globally**

- **Ramsar Convention Designation**: The Ramsar Secretariat designated Uttar Pradesh's **Surha Taal Bird Sanctuary** as a Wetland of International Importance.
- **Geographical & Environmental Profile**:
  - Located in **Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh**; covers 45 villages; notified in 1991 and renamed **Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary** in 2002.
  - Formed as a natural perennial **oxbow lake** created by an ancient meander of the **Ganga River**, situated between the Ganga and Saryu rivers.
- **India's Global & Regional Ramsar Standing**:
  - **Rank 1 in Asia**: India holds the highest number of Ramsar sites across the entire Asian continent.
  - **Rank 3 Globally**: Behind the **United Kingdom (176 sites)** and **Mexico (144 sites)**.
  - **Top 3 Indian States by Ramsar Sites**:
    1. **Tamil Nadu**: 20 Ramsar wetlands (highest in India).
    2. **Uttar Pradesh**: 13 Ramsar sites (second highest).
    3. **Odisha**: 6 Ramsar sites (third highest).
  - India's first designated Ramsar sites (1981): **Chilika Lake** (Odisha) and **Keoladeo National Park** (Rajasthan).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Newest Ramsar Site: **Surha Taal / Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary** (Ballia district, UP).
- Lake Hydrology: Natural perennial **oxbow lake** of the Ganga River.
- State Ramsar Ranks: **Tamil Nadu (20)** > **Uttar Pradesh (13)** > **Odisha (6)**.
- Global Standing: India is **#1 in Asia** and **#3 globally** (after UK & Mexico).

[JUN-049] **MCA Expands Schedule VII: CSR Funds Permitted in Social Stock Exchange ZCZP Instruments**

- **Regulatory Harmonization**: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (**MCA**) amended **Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013**, officially allowing corporate CSR expenditure to flow into the Social Stock Exchange (**SSE**) ecosystem.
- **Eligible CSR Conduit**:
  - Direct subscription to **Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) Instruments** issued by registered Not-for-Profit Organisations (NPOs) and listed on recognized Social Stock Exchanges is now legally recognized as eligible CSR spending under Schedule VII.
- **Statutory CSR Applicability Framework (Section 135)**:
  - Mandatory for companies having:
    - **Net Worth ≥ ₹500 crore**, OR
    - **Turnover ≥ ₹1,000 crore**, OR
    - **Net Profit ≥ ₹5 crore** during the immediately preceding financial year.
  - Mandatory allocation: At least **2% of the average net profits** made during the 3 immediately preceding financial years.
  - **Proposed Reform**: The *Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026* proposes doubling the net profit threshold from **₹5 crore to ₹10 crore** to reduce compliance overhead for small enterprises.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Eligible CSR Asset: **Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) instruments** listed on Social Stock Exchanges (SSE).
- Schedule Amended: **Schedule VII** of the *Companies Act, 2013*.
- Current Net Profit Threshold: **≥₹5 crore** (proposed hike to **₹10 crore** in 2026 Bill).
- Mandatory CSR Percentage: **2%** of average net profits of preceding 3 financial years.

[JUN-052] **Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) Elevated to India's 29th Navratna CPSE**

- **Corporate Governance Upgradation**: The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE, Ministry of Finance) and the Ministry of Defence officially elevated Kolkata-headquartered shipyard **Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE)** to **Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE)** status.
- **Historic Institutional Milestone**:
  - GRSE becomes India's **29th Navratna CPSE**, transitioning from its previous Miniratna Category-I classification.
  - **Enhanced Financial Autonomy**: Empowers the GRSE Board of Directors to make autonomous capital expenditures up to **₹1,000 crore** (or **15% of net worth** on a single project, whichever is lower) without seeking prior approval from the Central Government.
  - Authorizes GRSE to establish overseas joint ventures, subsidiaries, and strategic technological alliances up to ₹1,000 crore.
- **Shipbuilding Heritage**:
  - Established in **1884** as a private shipyard on the Hooghly River, nationalized by the Government of India in **1960**.
  - Constructed and delivered India's very first indigenous warship, **INS Ajay**, in **1961**.
  - Concurrently, Prime Minister Narendra Modi commissioned three GRSE-built naval assets at the Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port in Kolkata: **INS Dunagiri** (Project 17A Nilgiri-class guided missile frigate), **INS Sanshodhak** (large survey vessel), and **INS Agray** (anti-submarine shallow water craft).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- New Navratna Status Rank: **29th Navratna CPSE** of India (Kolkata-based).
- Autonomy Investment Limit: Up to **₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth** per project.
- Historical Warship: Built India's first indigenous warship **INS Ajay in 1961**.
- Commissioned Fleet: **INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak, INS Agray** (SMP Port, Kolkata).

[JUN-059] **FCI Expands Farm-to-Depot QR Code Tagging of Foodgrain Bags across AP, Telangana & Odisha**

- **Supply Chain Digitalization**: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution expanded the mandatory **Quick Response (QR) code tagging initiative** for all foodgrain bags procured and distributed by the **Food Corporation of India (FCI)**.
- **State Rollout Footprint**:
  - Formally scaled across three major paddy-producing and consuming states: **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha** during the ongoing marketing season.
  - Built upon successful technological pilot validations: the rice QR-tagging pilot conducted in Andhra Pradesh (December 2025 – January 2026) and the wheat QR-tagging pilot conducted in Punjab (April – May 2026).
- **Anti-Pilferage & Traceability Architecture**:
  - Each gunny bag is imprinted with a unique encrypted 2D QR code detailing procurement centre (mandi), mill code, moisture level, grain variety, date of bagging, and destination FCI silo/depot.
  - Prevents recycling of PDS foodgrains, eliminates phantom milling, and ensures real-time end-to-end inventory auditing on the Anna Darpan logistics platform.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Expanded States for FCI QR Tagging: **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha**.
- Previous Pilot States: **Andhra Pradesh** (rice) and **Punjab** (wheat).
- Administrative Entity: **Food Corporation of India (FCI)** under MoCA,F&PD.
- Core Objective: Real-time inventory tracing and elimination of diversion/recycling in PDS.

[JUN-060] **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6): Total Fertility Rate Stable at 2.0 & Rotavirus Coverage at 85.4%**

- **Demographic & Public Health Accounting**: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare released comprehensive analytical findings from the **6th National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6 2023–24)**:
- **Demographic Transition & Contraception**:
  - **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**: Remained stable at **2.0 children per woman**, securely positioned below the national replacement-level fertility benchmark of **2.1**.

  - **Full Immunization Coverage (cards)**: Scaled from 83.8% to **87.1%**; over **95.6%** of all vaccinations administered through public health institutions.
  - **Rotavirus Vaccine Coverage**: Registered a historic surge from 36.4% to **85.4%**, drastically curbing childhood diarrhoea.
  - **Measles Second Dose (MCV-2)**: Increased from 58.6% to **71.8%**.
  - Prevalence of Acute Respiratory Infections (ARI) dropped from 2.8% to 1.9%; severe childhood diarrhoea declined to 0.5%.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR): **2.0** (below replacement level of 2.1).
- Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (CPR): **69.1%** (up from 66.7%).
- Rotavirus Vaccine Surge: Reached **85.4%** (from 36.4%).
- Full Immunization Coverage: **87.1%** (with 95.6% delivered via public facilities).

[JUL-007] **RBI Master Circular on Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA) for Cross-Border Trade Settlement**

- **Consolidated Regulatory Architecture**: Reserve Bank of India issued a comprehensive Master Circular consolidating all directions governing **Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA)** issued between 2022 and 2025 under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA).
- **Core Operational Directives**:
  - **Account Opening & Approvals**: Authorised Dealer (AD Category-I) banks are permitted to open SRVAs for partner foreign banks after obtaining prior approval from the Foreign Exchange Department, Central Office of RBI.
  - **Denomination & Invoicing**: All export and import contracts settled via the mechanism must be **invoiced and denominated strictly in Indian Rupees (INR)**.
  - **Market-Determined Exchange Rates**: Currency conversion between INR and partner foreign currencies takes place at market-driven exchange rates rather than administratively pegged corridors.
  - **Settlement Process**: Indian importers making payments through this mechanism credit the invoice amount in INR into the SRVA of the correspondent overseas bank against bills of lading; Indian exporters are paid directly in INR from the balances in the SRVA.
  - **Surplus Rupee Balance Deployment**: Overseas banks holding surplus INR balances in SRVAs are permitted to invest funds in **Government Treasury Bills (T-Bills)**, sovereign G-Secs, and designated local bank deposits.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Account Type: **Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA)** allows foreign correspondent banks to hold INR balances in Indian AD banks.
- Currency Mandate: Trade invoices must be denominated in **Indian Rupees (INR)**.
- Permitted Investment of Surplus: Surplus balances can be invested in **Government Treasury Bills and Sovereign G-Secs** (not equities or unapproved corporate bonds).
- Strategic Impact: Critical vehicle for the **internationalisation of the Indian Rupee** and bilateral dedollarisation.

---48:T5247,[JUL-008] **RBI Master Direction — Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters (July 30)**

- **Scope & Applicability**: Applicable to all Scheduled Commercial Banks (incl. RRBs), All-India Financial Institutions (NABARD, EXIM, SIDBI, NHB), NBFCs, and Co-operative Banks.
- **Categorization Thresholds**:
  - **Wilful Defaulter**: Borrower or guarantor with an outstanding aggregate balance of **₹25 lakh and above**, who has defaulted despite having repayment capacity, siphoned/diverted funds, or disposed of charged assets without lender knowledge.
  - **Large Defaulter**: Borrower with an outstanding aggregate balance of **₹1 crore and above**, whose account is classified as Doubtful or Loss (or has been resolved via compromise/suit).
- **Mandatory Timelines for Lenders**:
  - Lenders must examine wilful default within **6 months of an account being classified as NPA**.
  - Identification Committee (Executive Director + two senior officials) issues a reasoned show cause notice allowing **21 days** for borrower response.
  - Review Committee (chaired by MD & CEO + two Independent Directors) confirms or cancels the classification.
- **Severe Regulatory Sanctions**:
  - **Credit Bar**: Barred from availing any fresh loan/credit facility from any institutional lender for **5 years** from the date their name is removed from the List of Wilful Defaulters.
  - **Corporate Bar**: Debarred from floating new ventures for 5 years and disqualified from serving as a Director on any corporate board under Section 164(2) of the Companies Act.
  - **Compromise Settlement Restriction**: No compromise or one-time settlement (OTS) allowed unless a mandatory cooling-off period of **12 months** has elapsed.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Threshold Trap: Wilful Defaulter = **₹25 lakh and above**; Large Defaulter = **₹1 crore and above** (classic IBPS/RBI trap).
- Timeline Trap: Lender must initiate wilful default examination within **6 months of NPA classification** (not 1 year).
- Penal Debarment: Bar on new credit is **5 years** after removal of name; compromise settlement cooling-off is **12 months**.

[JUL-009] **RBI Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Regulated Entities (July 15)**

- **Scope**: Replaced the legacy 2016 framework; issued across three distinct directions for Commercial Banks (incl. RRBs), Co-operative Banks, and NBFCs.
- **Compliance with Supreme Court Mandate (*SBI vs. Rajesh Agarwal, 2023*)**:
  - Lenders must strictly adhere to the **Principles of Natural Justice** (*Audi Alteram Partem* — hear the other side).
  - Mandatory issuance of a detailed, reasoned **Show Cause Notice (SCN)** giving the borrower a minimum of **21 calendar days** to submit a written representation before classifying an account as 'Fraud'.
- **Board-Level Oversight (SCBF)**:
  - Mandatory constitution of a **Special Committee of the Board on Monitoring and Follow-up of Frauds (SCBF)**, comprising independent and non-executive directors.
  - Dedicated Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG) at the executive level.
- **Reporting & Registry Norms**:
  - Lenders must report fraud cases to the **Central Fraud Registry (CFR)** within **21 days of classification**.
  - Mandatory reporting to Law Enforcement Agencies (State Police / CBI) based on threshold: Frauds >₹3 crore by private/foreign banks to CBI/SFIO; PSU banks follow CVC guidelines.
- **Early Warning Signals (EWS)**: Mandatory implementation of 42 EWS indicators for all borrower credit exposures of **₹50 crore and above**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Landmark Precedent: Rooted in the Supreme Court judgment *State Bank of India & Ors. vs. Rajesh Agarwal & Ors.*
- Notice Window: Minimum **21 days** given to the borrower to reply to SCN before fraud classification.
- Reporting Deadline: Classification must be uploaded to RBI's Central Fraud Registry (CFR) within **21 days**.
- EWS Exposure Threshold: Mandatory for accounts **≥₹50 crore**.

- **Policy Shift**: Authorized Dealer (AD Category-I) banks are permitted to facilitate remittances by resident individuals to International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, under the **Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)**.

[JUL-011] **RBI Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs)**

- **Regulatory Reach**: Extended to all Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks categorized under **Tier 3 (deposits ₹100 crore to ₹1,000 crore)** and **Tier 4 (deposits >₹1,000 crore)**.
- **Three Core Financial Health Indicators**:
  1. **Capital Adequacy (CRAR)**: Mandatory minimum is 9% for Tier 3 UCBs and 12% for Tier 4 UCBs.
  2. **Asset Quality (Net NPA Ratio)**: Breaching Net NPA **> 6.0%** triggers Risk Threshold 1.
  3. **Profitability (Return on Assets - RoA)**: Negative RoA for two consecutive financial years triggers mandatory supervisory intervention.
- **Mandatory Corrective Invocations**:
  - **Risk Threshold 1**: Restrictions on dividend payout/profit distribution and mandatory capital restoration plan.
  - **Risk Threshold 2**: Complete ban on opening new branches, expansion of business lines, and restriction on capital expenditure.
  - **Risk Threshold 3**: Discretionary RBI powers to supersede the Board of Directors, enforce amalgamation/merger, or cancel banking license.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Tier Applicability: Applicable only to **Tier 3 and Tier 4 UCBs** (deposits exceeding ₹100 crore); Tier 1 and Tier 2 UCBs are excluded.
- Net NPA Trigger: Net NPA crossing **6.0%** triggers PCA.
- Tier 4 Capital Rule: Tier 4 UCBs must maintain minimum CRAR of **12%** (vs. 9% for others).

[JUL-012] **RBI Revised Framework on Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) & Cash KYC (July 24)**

- **Context**: Comprehensive overhaul of domestic cash transfers through Business Correspondents (BCs), digital wallets, and prepaid payment instruments (PPIs) to curb illicit financial flows and mule accounts.
- **Mandatory Remitter Identification**:
  - Business correspondents and banking agents cannot execute cash-to-account remittances without **registering the remitter**.
  - Mandatory verification of remitter's mobile phone number using a one-time password (OTP) and validation of Officially Valid Documents (OVD) or Aadhaar e-KYC.
- **Transaction Limits Preserved**:
  - Maximum cash remittance limit remains **₹50,000 per month per remitter**.
  - Single cash transaction capped at **₹5,000** for non-KYC walk-in customers at BC outlets.
- **Beneficiary Verification**: Banks must include remitter identification details in the payment message (IMPS/NEFT/UPI) sent to the destination beneficiary bank to ensure end-to-end auditability.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Monthly Cash Limit: ₹50,000 per remitter per month.
- Core Regulatory Mandate: Mandatory remitter mobile OTP verification and OVD registration for all cash remittances at BC points.

[JUL-013] **RBI Directives on Dividend Declaration by Commercial Banks**

- **Prudential Standards**: Revised framework specifying parameters commercial banks must satisfy to declare dividends on equity shares or remit profits (in the case of foreign bank branches).
- **Three Minimum Pre-requisites**:
  1. **CRAR**: Minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio of at least **11.5%** (inclusive of 2.5% Capital Conservation Buffer) for each of the preceding three financial years.
  2. **Net NPA**: Net NPA ratio must be **less than 6.0%** for the financial year for which dividend is proposed.
  3. **Supervisory Compliance**: Bank must comply with RBI regulations on transfer to Statutory Reserve Fund (min 20% of net profits) and provisioning.
- **Dividend Payout Ratio Matrix**:
  - Net NPA = 0%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is **50%**.
  - Net NPA between 0% and 1%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is **40%**.
  - Net NPA between 5% and 6%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is **10%**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Net NPA Ceiling: Must be **<6%** to be eligible for any dividend payout.
- Minimum CRAR: Must be at least **11.5%** for preceding 3 consecutive years.
- Maximum Payout Cap: **50%** of net profit (only for zero Net NPA banks).

[JUL-014] **Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) & Mandatory CERSAI Registration**

- **Statutory Framework**: Governed under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, and the Factoring Regulation Act, 2011, providing non-recourse digital discounting of MSME trade receivables.
- **Mandatory CERSAI Registration**:
  - All Factoring Units (invoices/bills of exchange) created and financed on TReDS platforms must be registered with **CERSAI** (Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India).
  - Registration prevents fraudulent dual-financing or pledging of the same receivable across multiple commercial lenders.
- **Operating Platforms in India**:
  - **RXIL** (Receivables Exchange of India Ltd — India's first operational TReDS exchange launched in 2016; joint venture of NSE and SIDBI).
  - **M1xchange** (Mynd Solutions Pvt. Ltd.).
  - **Invoicemart** (A.TREDS Ltd. — Axis Bank & mjunction).
  - **C2treds** (C2FO Factoring Solutions Pvt. Ltd.).
  - **DTX** (KredX Platform Pvt. Ltd.).
- **Net Worth Mandate**: Existing RBI-authorized TReDS operators must ramp up their statutory minimum net worth to **₹25 crore** by **March 31, 2028** (extended compliance glide path from the initial proposed 2027 window).
- **Eligible Participants**: Buyers (corporates, CPSEs, government departments), Sellers (MSMEs), and Financiers (banks, NBFC factors).

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Fraud Prevention: Mandatory registration with **CERSAI** eliminates duplicate invoice financing.
- First TReDS Platform: **RXIL** (commenced operations in 2016; NSE + SIDBI JV).
- Net Worth Deadline: Existing operators must achieve **₹25 crore net worth by 31 March 2028**.
- Ineligible Participants: Stock exchanges and insurance underwriters cannot participate as financiers on TReDS.

[JUL-016] **SEBI Depository Investor Protection Fund (IPF) Norms: Operational Expense Utilization Capped at 5%**

- **Regulatory Framework & Effective Date**: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) amended norms governing Investor Protection Funds (IPF) maintained by depositories (NSDL and CDSL), permitting depositories to utilize **up to 5% of annual interest or income** earned from the IPF corpus for administrative and operational expenses, effective **September 2026**.
- **Eligible Operating Outlays**:
  - Remuneration and salaries of dedicated personnel employed directly by the independent IPF Trust.
  - Statutory compliance expenditures, including independent audit fees, taxation, and Charity Commissioner registration fees.
- **Corpus Protection Invariant**:
  - At least **95% of the annual income/interest** generated by the fund must be compulsorily credited back to replenish the principal IPF corpus.
  - In case administrative expenses exceed the 5% threshold, the deficit must be absorbed entirely by the depository from its own corporate balance sheet, not from the IPF principal.
  - Unutilized portions of the 5% allowance cannot be carried forward as profit and must revert to the corpus.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Permitted Expense Cap: Maximum **5% of annual interest/income** from the IPF corpus (not 5% of the total corpus).
- Mandatory Replenishment: At least **95% of annual income** must be added back into the principal fund.
- Deficit Bearing: Any expense exceeding the 5% ceiling must be borne **by the depository itself**.

[JUL-017] **SEBI Reintroduces Open-Market Share Buybacks via Stock Exchanges; Freezes Promoter ISINs**

- **Policy Reversal & Streamlining**: SEBI formally reintroduced corporate share buybacks conducted through the secondary stock exchange trading window, effective **August 1, 2026**.
- **Core Prudential Parameters**:
  - **Aggregate Quantum Cap**: Share buybacks via the open-market exchange route are capped at **less than 15%** of the company's total paid-up equity capital and free reserves (tested against both standalone and consolidated balance sheets).
  - **Drastic Execution Compression**: The buyback window must open within **4 working days** of the public announcement and must be fully concluded within **66 working days** (drastically reduced from the erstwhile 6-month timeline).
  - **Promoter Share Freezing**: To prevent front-running, manipulation, and insider offloading, promoter group shareholdings are **frozen at the depository ISIN level** throughout the entire buyback duration.
  - **Merchant Banker Option**: Appointment of a merchant banker for open-market buybacks is made optional, placing direct compliance accountability on the corporate board.
  - **Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS)**: Companies are strictly prohibited from announcing buyback volumes that would reduce post-offer public shareholding below the statutory **25% MPS threshold**.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Open-Market Buyback Cap: Strictly **less than 15%** of paid-up capital and free reserves.
- Execution Timeline: Opens within **4 working days** and closes within **66 working days** (earlier 6 months).
- Promoter Lock: Promoters' holdings are **frozen at the ISIN level** for the duration of the buyback.
- Statutory Limit: Cannot breach the **25% Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS)** requirement.

[JUL-019] **SEBI Authorises Intraday Borrowing Window for Mutual Funds to Bridge Same-Day Settlement Gaps**

- **Liquidity Management Relaxation**: SEBI permitted Asset Management Companies (AMCs) to access intraday borrowing credit lines to resolve temporary same-day cash flow mismatches arising from lumpy redemption pressures and delayed banking settlement legs.
- **Operational Boundaries**:
  - **Permitted Uses**: Strictly confined to meeting intraday redemption payouts, dividend/interest distributions, settlement of underlying market purchases, mark-to-market (MTM) margin calls, and foreign exchange settlement legs.
  - **End-of-Day Repayment Invariant**: AMCs must ensure that **100% of intraday borrowings are fully extinguished and repaid before the close of the trading day**.
  - **Zero Cost Transfer to Unit-Holders**: Unit-holders cannot be charged for intraday facility expenses; any interest cost, commitment fee, or losses resulting from delays in receiving anticipated funds must be borne **exclusively by the AMC**, not the scheme.
  - **Board Governance**: AMCs must formulate an independent Board-approved policy on intraday credit limits and publish the operational architecture on their official portals.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Repayment Mandate: Intraday borrowings must be repaid **before the end of the same trading day**.
- Expense Liability: Costs must be absorbed **100% by the AMC** (zero cost transfer to mutual fund unit-holders).
- Allowed Facility: Designed strictly to service intraday liquidity timing gaps against expected same-day inflows.

Nair (former Chief General Manager, State Bank of India)** as the Official Liquidator.
- **Statutory Enforcement Background**:
  - Followed the statutory cancellation of PPBL's banking licence by the Reserve Bank of India on **April 24, 2026** under **Section 22(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** due to chronic supervisory non-compliance and AML KYC deficiencies.
  - Proceeding executed jointly under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and Section 271/272 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- **Institutional Context of Payment Banks in India**:
  - Conceived on the recommendations of the **Nachiket Mor Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services (2013)** to advance micro-savings and digital remittances.
  - Operational Rules: Minimum paid-up capital of ₹100 crore; demand deposits capped at **₹2,00,000 per individual customer**; permitted to issue debit cards but **strictly prohibited from lending, issuing credit cards, or accepting time deposits**.
  - Active Surviving Entities: Airtel Payments Bank (first to launch, 2016), India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Fino Payments Bank, Jio Payments Bank, and NSDL Payments Bank.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Statutory Power: Banking licence cancelled under **Section 22(4) of Banking Regulation Act 1949**.
- Committee Genesis: Payment Banks conceptualized by the **Nachiket Mor Committee (2013)**.
- Deposit Ceiling: Maximum balance of **₹2,00,000 per customer**.
- Regulatory Restriction: Payment Banks can issue **Debit Cards ONLY**; strictly barred from lending, advances, and credit card issuance.

[JUL-023] **Payment System Metrics: The Great Credit vs. Debit Card Divergence**

- **Debit Card Volume & Value Contraction**:
  - Debit card transaction volume collapsed precipitously from **408.7 crore to 133.6 crore** transactions.
  - Debit card transaction spend contracted from **₹7.4 lakh crore down to ₹4.5 lakh crore**.
  - **Primary Driver**: Mass consumer migration to **UPI** for daily merchant payments and low-ticket POS transactions.
- **Credit Card Growth Trajectory**:
  - Total annual credit card spend crossed **₹18.8 lakh crore**, growing at an annual rate exceeding **25%**.
  - Fueled by e-commerce penetration, travel rewards, cashback incentives, and RuPay credit cards on UPI.
- **Banking Sector Market Share in Credit Cards**:
  - **Private Sector Banks**: Share in outstanding credit cards surged from **67.7% to 71.1%**, controlling over seven-tenths of the national market.
  - **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)**: Maintained a steady footprint between **23.5% and 23.9%** (anchored by SBI Cards).
  - **Foreign Banks**: Footprint contracted sharply from **9.3% down to 3.8%** following multinational retail banking portfolio sales.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Contraction Root Cause: Debit card drop is driven by **UPI adoption** (not ATM closures or regulatory bans).
- Market Dominance: Private sector banks issue **71.1%** of credit cards; Foreign banks declined to **3.8%**.
- Benchmark Figures: Credit card spend = **₹18.8 lakh crore**; Debit card spend dropped to **₹4.5 lakh crore**.

[JUL-025] **RBI Prohibits Bank SMS Alert Charges for Compliance & Promos; Makes Alerts Below ₹500 Optional**

- **Customer Protection Directive**: Reserve Bank of India directed all Scheduled Commercial Banks, Payment Banks, and Small Finance Banks to immediately cease levying quarterly SMS alert fees on account holders for mandatory compliance notices, financial literacy alerts, or promotional broadcasts.
- **Industry Financial Impact**:
  - Banks historically deducted between **₹15 to ₹18 per quarter plus GST** from active savings accounts, generating an estimated cumulative fee revenue of over **₹300 crore annually**.
  - A large commercial bank servicing an active base of 50 million savings accounts faces an annual non-interest fee contraction of approximately **₹360 crore**.
- **Operational Transaction Alert Threshold**:
  - To prevent unnecessary notification spam and reduce telecom transmission expenses, RBI clarified that automated transactional SMS alerts for debit transactions valued at **₹500 or less are now optional** (at the bank's discretion or customer opt-in).
  - High-value debit transaction notifications, critical OTPs, and unauthorized debit warning prompts remain mandatory and must be delivered free of charge.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Prohibited Fee: Levying quarterly charges for regulatory, awareness, and promotional SMS messages.
- Discretionary Alert Ceiling: Transactional SMS alerts for amounts **≤ ₹500** are made optional.
- Historic Baseline Fee: Banks earlier charged **₹15–₹18 per quarter**.

---4a:T1d13,[JUL-026] **Historic Legal Transition: Three New Criminal Laws Enacted Nationwide (July 1)**

- **Enforcement Date**: Three transformative criminal law statutes came into full legal effect across India on **July 1, 2024**, completely repealing and replacing British colonial-era penal codes:
  1. **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)**: Replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
  2. **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS)**: Replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).
  3. **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA)**: Replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
- **Key Judicial Innovations**:
  - Mandates **Zero FIR** (can be filed at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction).
  - Introduction of **e-FIR** and compulsory electronic summons via SMS/WhatsApp.
  - Mandatory audio-video recording of search and seizure operations, and mandatory forensic investigation for offences punishable by **7 years or more**.
  - Introduction of **Community Service** as a recognized formal penal punishment for minor offences.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Enforcement Date: **July 1, 2024** (not Jan 1 or April 1).
- Statutory Cross-Mapping: BNS = IPC; BNSS = CrPC; BSA = Evidence Act.
- Forensic Threshold: Mandatory for offences carrying imprisonment of **7 years or more**.

[JUL-028] **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act & Implementing Rules Enacted**

- **Statutory Enforcement**: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions operationalized the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024** and notified its comprehensive implementing rules nationwide.
- **Examinations & Bodies Covered**:
  - Covers competitive examinations conducted by Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), National Testing Agency (NTA), and the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (**IBPS**).
- **Penal Slabs & Liability Architecture**:
  - **Individual Malpractices**: Persons resorting to unfair means face imprisonment of **3 to 5 years** and a fine up to **₹10 lakh**.
  - **Organized Paper Leak Syndicates**: Imprisonment of **5 to 10 years** and a mandatory minimum fine of **₹1 crore**.
  - **Service Provider Penalty**: Examination conducting agencies/service providers found complicit face recovery of full examination costs and a complete bar from conducting public examinations for **4 years**.
  - **Legal Character**: All offences under the statute are non-bailable, cognizable, and non-compoundable.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Banking Exam Coverage: Explicitly governs **IBPS** examinations alongside UPSC, SSC, and NTA.
- Organized Syndicate Penalties: Minimum fine of **₹1 Crore**; 5 to 10 years imprisonment.
- Legal Classification: **Cognizable and Non-Bailable** offences.

  - Developed by CSIR–Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CSIR-CIMFR), Dhanbad.
  - Utilizes concentrated microalgae cultures in a mobile photobioreactor column to absorb carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) and discharge pure oxygen at rates equivalent to 10–20 mature urban trees; deployed at CIMFR Dhanbad and Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) Singrauli.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Green Chemical: **HFO-1234yf** developed by **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad** with Global Warming Potential **GWP < 1**.
- International Treaty: Replaces HFCs pursuant to the **Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol**.
- Carbon Capture Tech: **Smart Algal Liquid Tree (SALT)** developed by **CSIR-CIMFR Dhanbad**.

- Tiger Census: India tiger count is **3,682** (75% of global total); Madhya Pradesh is the 'Tiger State' (785 tigers).

[JUL-042] **National Fish Farmers’ Day (July 10) & PMMSY Blue Economy Milestones**

- **Historical Significance**: Observed annually on **July 10** commemorating the pioneering scientific breakthrough by **Dr. Hiralal Chaudhuri and Dr. K.H. Alikunhi**, who successfully demonstrated induced breeding (hypophysation) in Indian Major Carps on July 10, 1957 in Angul, Odisha.
- **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) Benchmarks**:
  - Flagship umbrella scheme under the Department of Fisheries (Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying) with an investment of **₹20,050 crore** over 5 years.
  - Production Milestone: India is the **2nd largest fish producing country** globally (~8% global share) and the world's leading exporter of farmed shrimp.
  - Target: Scaling national fisheries exports to **₹1 lakh crore** and generating over 55 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities.
- **Digital Enablers**: Operationalization of the **Matsya Setu** mobile learning app and the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) to advance formal credit and insurance access to fishers.

**EXAM ANGLE:**

- Observed Date: **July 10** (honors Dr. Hiralal Chaudhuri & Dr. K.H. Alikunhi's 1957 hypophysation breakthrough).
- Global Fish Rank: India is the **2nd largest fish producer** in the world (~8% share).
